titulo: Dativo de interés: me, te, le... for who wins or loses
subtitulo: Me robaron la cartera. Se me escapó el perro.
regla: An indirect object pronoun can mark the person affected by an event, for good or bad, even if they aren't the receiver: Nos cayó un aguacero = it poured on us; Me robaron la cartera = they stole my wallet (from me). Sometimes it's ambiguous: ¡Nos compraron la casa! = for us or from us.

bloques.texto: **me, te, le, nos, les** mark someone who **gains or loses** because of what happens.
English uses _on me, from me, for me_ or a possessive: **me robaron la cartera** = _they stole my wallet_.
Spanish prefers the pronoun + article over a possessive for things that belong to someone: **me rayaron el carro**, not ~~rayaron mi carro~~ (possible but less natural).
It can be **ambiguous**: **nos compraron la casa** = _bought it for us_ or _bought it from us_.
Mexico uses it a lot with family affection: **no me le hagas caso**, **cuídamelo**.
Tip: the pronoun answers _who felt it?_

lista.en: Yesterday we got caught in a downpour.

lista.es: Ese niño un día ==me robó== la cartera.
lista.en: That kid stole my wallet one day.

lista.es: No te preocupes, ==te van a llover== ofertas de trabajo.
lista.en: Don't worry, job offers are going to pour in for you.

lista.es: ==Me le== pones mucha atención a la niña, ¿eh?
lista.en: You pay close attention to the girl for me, okay?
They bought us the house! / They bought our house!

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _The baby got sick on us._

lista.r: They sold the store to him, or they sold his store.
